purpose: 15 separate statutory/constitutional initiatives for 2028: property tax levy limits and voter approval to exceed them, ban on unfunded mandates, 'Harvest Fuel Tax Holiday' (2-month annual fuel tax suspension plus 35-cent cap), education and election administration.
sponsor: Eric Underwood (Lincoln, former Nebraska GOP chair) / Advocates for All Nebraskans
circulation_firm: A new Nebraska-based signature-gathering firm, name not disclosed, using only Nebraska circulators
signatures_required: Statutory: 7% of registered voters; constitutional: 10% of registered voters; plus 5% in at least 38 of 93 counties (exact counts unknown for 2028)
evidence_note: Nebraska Examiner (Oct 16, 2026) reports launch after Nov 3; wording still under Revisor of Statutes review. Plans door-to-door canvassing from a 200,000+ voter list across ~150 cities. Article says a new Nebraska-only signature firm will assist, so paid circulation is likely, but pay is not confirmed. Same group submitted no signatures for its 2026 petitions. Watch for legislation from Gov. Pillen and SOS Evnen to ban per-signature pay and require circulators to be citizens (see 1011now, Sept 3, 2026).

campaign_name: Tax Relief Nebraska – online sports betting (constitutional + statutory)
purpose: Legalize and regulate online sports betting; statutory framework sends 70% of tax proceeds to property tax relief
sponsor: Tax Relief Nebraska (led by WarHorse casino with online sportsbook operators and local investors)
signatures_collected: 201,000+ (constitutional) and ~146,000 (statutory), as submitted, not verified counts
budget_or_spend: DraftKings and FanDuel gave about $3.5M each (more than $7M combined) per Nebraska Public Media, June 26, 2026
decision_maker: unknown (Lynne McNally, WarHorse director of government relations, is the public spokesperson)
evidence_note: Drive finished with signatures submitted in late June / July 2026. McNally said paid circulators are necessary for a successful drive. Nebraska law allows per-signature pay and out-of-state circulators. Firm name not found; the NADC filings were not checked. Final ballot certification not confirmed in the sources read.

purpose: Constitutional amendment raising the legislative vote needed to change voter-approved initiatives from 2/3 to 4/5, and applying it to laws affecting the initiative process
sponsor: Respect Nebraska Voters coalition; ballot sponsor Dawn Essink (Omaha Together One Community)
signatures_required: 10% of registered voters plus 5% in 38 counties (exact count not given in the source)
evidence_note: Signatures submitted July 2, 2026, with signers in every county. Whether circulators were paid is not stated, and qualification was not confirmed in the sources read.

purpose: Require an 80% legislative vote plus a statewide vote to change voter-approved initiatives; bar the legislature from restricting the initiative process
signatures_required: 5% of the gubernatorial vote in 6 of 8 congressional districts (~170,215 minimum depending on distribution)
evidence_note: This was the only citizen initiative to submit signatures for Missouri's 2026 ballot. The Missouri Supreme Court placed it on the Nov 3 ballot as Amendment 6 (Sept 3, 2026). Firm and pay were not found.

campaign_name: People Not Politicians – referendum on 2025 congressional map
purpose: Veto referendum to overturn the congressional map passed Sept 12, 2025
sponsor: People Not Politicians (PAC); executive director Richard von Glahn
signatures_required: About 110,000 valid (5% of voters in 6 of 8 congressional districts)
evidence_note: Labor Tribune says the drive used paid petition circulators alongside labor volunteers, and that outside groups allegedly offered paid circulators $5,000 to $30,000 to dump signatures. The Missouri Supreme Court put the referendum on the Nov 2026 ballot. The drive is finished. Firm and pay rate were not found.

purpose: Constitutional amendment making public education a fundamental right
sponsor: Missouri Right to Education campaign (director Spencer Toder); Missouri NEA pledged 'substantial support' for 2028
signatures_required: Constitutional threshold: 8% of the gubernatorial vote in 6 of 8 congressional districts (exact 2028 figure unknown)
deadline: unknown (2028 cycle; Missouri initiative deadlines are typically early May of the election year)
signatures_collected: About 35,000 in the abandoned 2026 attempt; 2028 count 0
evidence_note: The 2026 drive was volunteer-led and stopped Mar 31, 2026 at roughly one-fifth of the needed signatures. The campaign plans to return in 2028 with MNEA backing. MNEA money makes this a candidate for a paid drive, but nothing is confirmed. The SOS 2028 petition page could not be fetched (not on the allowlist), so 2028 filing status is unknown.

campaign_name: SQ 836 – Open primaries (Vote Yes 836 / Oklahoma United)
purpose: Replace closed partisan primaries with a single top-two primary
sponsor: Oklahoma United / Oklahomans United for Progress (founder Margaret Kobos)
signatures_collected: Over 200,000 submitted; SOS counted 142,567 valid (57,841 tossed under the 2024 data-match law)
evidence_note: Circulation ran Oct 29, 2025 to Jan 2026. Ruled short of signatures; a challenge was heard by a Supreme Court referee July 14, 2026, and the outcome was not found. Paid circulation is not mentioned in the sources. It could need a new drive if it loses.

purpose: Phase out ad valorem taxes on owner-occupied homesteads by 2029
sponsor: Sen. Shane Jett, Rep. Jay Steagall, former Rep. Mike Reynolds
evidence_note: Filed Jan 12, 2026. On Oct 7, 2026 the Oklahoma Supreme Court ruled it unconstitutional before circulation. Sponsors may refile a redrafted version; none was found.

sponsor: Oklahomans for Responsible Cannabis Action (ORCA); director Jed Green
evidence_note: Failed to qualify in Nov 2025. It was the first drive under SB 1027's county-cap law. Included as a possible refile prospect only.

campaign_name: Dakotans for Health – initiative-process protection measures
purpose: (1) Require voter approval for legislative changes to initiative/referendum procedures; (2) for 7 years after passage, changes to voter-approved measures need a 3/4 legislative vote plus voter approval
sponsor: Dakotans for Health (co-founder Rick Weiland); attorney Jim Leach
signatures_required: unknown (not stated in the sources read)
deadline: Disputed: SOS says May 5, 2026 passed with no citizen measures filed; the 8th Circuit struck the Feb deadline law Aug 11, 2026; AG Jackley is seeking rehearing en banc
evidence_note: Both measures were approved for circulation 3/27/2025. In May 2026 the group was still collecting signatures after the deadline, arguing there is no valid deadline. The legal status of the deadline is unresolved. Whether circulators are paid is not stated, and current circulation as of Oct 2026 is not confirmed. A strong 2028 prospect if the 2026 path closes.

campaign_name: South Dakotans for Fair Taxes – SB 245 referendum
purpose: Refer SB 245 (Homeowner Property Tax Reduction Fund, sales-tax-for-property-tax swap) to voters
type: Statewide referendum on a state law
sponsor: South Dakotans for Fair Taxes (Bread for the World SD, SD AFL-CIO, Dakota Rural Action)
evidence_note: Petition approved 4/29/2026; failed June 29, 2026. The group says it will pursue the issue in the 2027 legislative session. Paid circulation was not mentioned.

campaign_name: Property tax replacement with 'retail transaction' tax
purpose: Repeal real property taxes and replace them with a retail transaction tax
signatures_collected: unknown (SOS reported no citizen measures submitted by May 5)
evidence_note: Approved for circulation 11/3/2025. The SOS said no citizen-led measures were submitted by May 5, 2026. Property tax issues are likely to return for 2028. The SD SOS page lists no 2028 petitions yet.

The ND SOS 'Petitions in Circulation' page shows 'None at this time' for initiated measures, referred measures and petitions under review. The SOS news page (Sept 21, 2026) mentions only the Nov 3 ballot guide. The 2026 general ballot has CM1 (HCR 3003, legislative) and CM2 (school lunch funding). Local and recall petitions were not searched.

campaign_name: Protect AR Rights – Ballot Measure Rights Amendment
purpose: Constitutional amendment protecting the right to initiative/referendum; bar the legislature from amending or repealing citizen amendments
sponsor: Protect AR Rights (ballot question committee; member org Arkansas Public Policy Panel, Exec. Dir. Bill Kopsky)
evidence_note: The AR SOS page lists 'None' citizen-initiated measures for the 2026 general election, so this measure apparently did not qualify (reason not found). A federal judgment (WD Ark., Aug 21, 2026) struck down some Arkansas initiative restrictions. No 2028 AG-certified ballot titles were found, and the paid canvasser registration list was not checked.

campaign_name: Save Dallas City Hall – charter amendment
purpose: Charter amendment naming 1500 Marilla as the seat of government and requiring an election before city operations leave City Hall
type: City charter amendment petition (for a possible May 2027 ballot)
sponsor: Save Dallas City Hall Coalition (supporters include attorney Ben Abbott, McDermott and Jonsson family descendants)
deadline: Collection from Oct 2, 2026 to mid-January 2027 per D Magazine (Fox 4 cites a 60-day window); exact date unknown
evidence_note: Notice of intent filed and drive launched Oct 2, 2026, so it is active now. With donor backing and 20,000 signatures needed, it is a good candidate for paid circulators, but no paid hiring was found. D Magazine (Oct 20, 2026) lists 4 Dallas petition drives, but the page could not be fetched, so the other 3 are not recorded.

campaign_name: Austin United PAC – convention center expansion petition
purpose: Force a public vote on the Austin convention center expansion
sponsor: Austin United PAC (attorneys Bill Bunch, Bobby Levinski)
evidence_note: The petition was rejected, and the district court upheld the rejection. In Feb 2026 the PAC said it was 'immediately organizing a new petition drive for a potential November election'. Whether that new drive happened is unknown. Austin thresholds: 20,000 for initiative, referendum or charter amendment.

Iowa has no statewide citizen initiative. Local, recall and ballot-access petitions were NOT searched because the shared web-search budget ran out before Iowa was reached. This is a research gap, not a confirmed absence.

Minnesota has no statewide citizen initiative. City charter petitions (e.g. Minneapolis, St. Paul), recalls and ballot access were NOT searched because the shared web-search budget ran out. This is a research gap, not a confirmed absence.

Kansas has no statewide citizen initiative. Local petitions (e.g. Wichita, Kansas City KS), recalls and new-party ballot access were NOT searched because the shared web-search budget ran out. This is a research gap, not a confirmed absence.
